title: Compute Stewardship Initiative — cross-cycle roadmap for dynamic batching, cache tiers, and quant profiles
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Initiative to coordinate cross-cycle work that reduces per-token compute cost while preserving latency SLOs and output quality. Scope includes: dynamic batching strategies (client+server presets), KV cache tiering and TTL policy, and curated quantization profiles for 4-bit/INT8 workflows. Outcomes: a prioritized roadmap, validated prototype(s) on representative workloads, rollout plan for Hosted and Dedicated, and observability dashboards tied to unit-econ KPIs.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end experiment plan for at least 3 customer workload classes (chat short, long-context, embeddings)
Validated prototype showing >=18% token-cost reduction on average for test corpus without >5% QoE regression
Dashboard with per-route token cost, latency P95, and fallback rate in Console; retention 90d
Rollout runbook and canary gating checks documented in Confluence with approval matrix
Quantization guardrails and recommended profiles published in model-catalog; default profile for new deployments

decisions: Adopt three-tier KV cache TTL (hot/warm/cold) with adaptive promotion heuristics based on per-route hit rates
Default quantization profile for small models = q4_dynamic; for large context models run A/B with q8 where latency SLO is strict
Batching presets: client_hint (latency) vs throughput_hint (cost) exposed in API and Console as named policies
Telemetry contract: emit token-level cost attribution and model-variant labels for each request

notes: Measurement plan emphasizes unit-econ (tokens/$), quality (task-level evals) and reliability (latency P95/P99). Risk areas: quant-induced quality regressions for embeddings, and backend kernel constraints. We will gate production rollouts on explicit quality thresholds and rollback windows.
